name: ElasticCard
description: Router card that expands from a resting column to a wide dark state. v2 architecture: State × Type axes, inverse-token dark surfaces (no Context axis).

props.name: state
props.description: Card state. resting = light column; expanded/mobile = dark inverse surface.

props.name: type
props.description: standard = ProductLockup header; featured = heading-6 text header. (Figma set default is featured; code defaults to standard for backward compatibility.)

props.name: heading
props.description: Featured header text; falls back to label.

props.name: product
props.description: ProductLockup prop overrides. context is ignored (v2 has no Context axis).

props.name: mediaSrc / mediaAlt / mediaTemplate / mediaAspect / mediaOverlay
props.description: Media zone content, same contract as v1.

knownTokenGaps: --s2a-color-surface-subtle / --s2a-color-surface-inverse-subtle / --s2a-color-surface-default — bound in Figma, not yet in the shipped tokens release; CSS chains to shipped background/* equivalents
--s2a-router-card-padding / --s2a-router-card-height-max — bound in Figma, not yet shipped; px fallbacks
Card widths (294 / 496 / 360) are unbound in Figma v2 — literals in CSS
deviations: Figma's State=mobile, Type=featured variant embeds a deprecated 48px 'ControlButton — v1' instance in the footer; code keeps the 24px header CTA puck for both types until that Figma inconsistency is resolved.
Hover on a resting card mirrors the expanded-state visuals (coded interaction; Figma models the states as separate variants).

notes: Decorative caret/CTA icons are aria-hidden; provide ariaLabel for interactive cards.
